messages.content: [Special education in the United Kingdom] Special education in the United Kingdom, as an aspect of education, is a devolved matter, with each of the countries of the United Kingdom having separate systems under separate governments. The UK Government is responsible for England, whilst the Scottish Government, the Welsh Government and the Northern Ireland Executive are responsible for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, respectively. Special education in Scotland is formally known as Additional Support Needs (ASN) or Additional Support for Learning (ASL) whereas in England it is usually referred to as 'Special educational needs' ('SEN'), or 'special educational needs and disabilities' ('SEND').
